Completed enrolment of the world's first-in-human study of graphene neural interfaces for brain decoding & mapping (tumour-resection surgery, Manchester)
Australian approval to begin the CYBORG first-in-human study of Phantom X, a subcutaneous sensor array (Cabrini Health, Melbourne). Study authorization, not a completed implantation.

Second fully implanted, fully wireless, full-function ('three-full') BCI clinical case: BCI-FES restored self-feeding and painting in a paralyzed patient, following the first such clinical implant at the end of 2025. April 23 is the company announcement date, not a specified procedure day.
APEX academic research partnership program announced with researchers at Stanford, Mass General, Pitt, UC Davis, and Michigan. This record describes the partnership, not an implantation.
FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for its Smart Neurostimulation System — first neurostim device designated for TBI-related memory loss
FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for the Occular visual cortical prosthesis; also grants access to the FDA's TAP pilot
MintNeuro partnership to advance miniature BCI therapy for mental health

Health Canada approval to launch CAN-PRIME at UHN (Toronto Western)

CE Mark for AlphaDBS (adaptive DBS, Parkinson's)

FDA IDE for Empower BP pivotal study of implanted ARC-IM (blood-pressure instability after SCI)
FDA IDE for Connect-One Early Feasibility Study of Connexus (speech + computer control)

Announced an FDA approval letter expanding the investigational Connect-One pathway through Convey to compatible personal laptops, tablets, and phones after an agreed deployment and testing process. Not marketing authorization or evidence of completed use on every device type.

Second FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for Brain Interchange, covering computer-cursor control for people with non-progressive quadriplegia. Distinct from the April stroke-rehabilitation designation.
First Connect-One participant used the fully implanted Connexus BCI for real-time speech and text, including open-ended questions. Investigational; not a marketing approval.
Series D raise of $250m, co-led by Pershing Square Inc. and the Ackman Oxman Institute. The release's $430m total capital raised is a cumulative figure and is not plotted.

Partnership with Mila to advance AI-powered neural interfaces and Neurosoft's cortical foundation model program. Neurosoft joins Mila's industry network; this is a research partnership, not a clinical efficacy result or regulatory approval.

Science announced the promotion of Chief Strategy Officer Darius Shahida to President. CEO Max Hodak cited his role in the Series C and European commercial launch of PRIMA. Date is the company announcement, not a separately disclosed effective date.

In a September 2026 exchange disclosure, Neuracle reported 13 NEO-ONE SCI systems sold since July 2026 and 8 implanted as of the reply. The linked body does not establish the filing day or individual sale/implant dates; no revenue or IPO proceeds are inferred.

Science announced two FDA Humanitarian Use Device designations for PRIMA: advanced geographic atrophy and Stargardt disease. July 22 is the announcement date, not the grant dates. HUD designation is not FDA marketing approval; a separate Humanitarian Device Exemption review is required.

Science's announcement of PRIMAvera 36-month follow-up results: 18 patients evaluable for efficacy and 27 for safety from 38 implanted. Company-reported mean gain of 29 ETDRS letters; 14 of 18 achieved at least a 15-letter improvement. Conference follow-up disclosure, not a new FDA approval or a claim about all 38 patients.

Science disclosed early rehabilitation progress for the first PRIMAlia participant with Stargardt disease at Sydney Eye Hospital (NCT07266584): a letter in the first session and a word in the second. Implantation was in May 2026; this is the disclosure date. Company-reported single-patient observation, not trial-wide efficacy or commercial authorization for Stargardt disease.

Paradromics and University of Michigan announced the first fully implanted Connexus participant in the Connect-One Early Feasibility Study (NCT07357428). This is the announcement date, not a separately disclosed surgery date. Distinct from the 2025 temporary intraoperative recording; Connexus remains investigational, not commercially approved.

Company-reported four-year preclinical durability milestone using two sheep with cortical modules representative of Connexus electrode technology. Disclosure date; stable longitudinal recording and decoding, not uninterrupted recording or four years of human use. A separate six-sheep full-platform study had nearly two years of follow-up.

Announced a preprint describing Layer 7 surface recordings from 70 patients across 12 academic centers, with more than 180 hours of synchronized neural and behavioral data. Separately, cumulative Precision system implants had surpassed 100 patients. Company-reported research disclosure, not 100 permanent implants or evidence of completed whole-brain coverage.

Announced a clinical research partnership with UChicago Medicine researchers on AI-driven sensorimotor function and neuroprosthetics. Research-network expansion using Layer 7; not a new FDA clearance, completed clinical efficacy result, or disclosed financing.

Neurosurgical Focus publication of Layer 7 intraoperative feasibility in four patients undergoing awake tumor surgery. Reported four-word speech classification of 77.5% and four-direction motor classification of 78–84%; the abstract does not specify the speech-task participant count. February 2026 is the publication month, not procedure dates. Small acute study, not unrestricted speech restoration or chronic implant efficacy.

Newronika reported the first ADVENT participant received an αDBS implant in Monza on September 21; the September 30 announcement marked the first pivotal-study procedure, not U.S. marketing approval or comparative study results.

Neuralink reported participants streamed over 50,000 hours of unlabeled neural data and participant-specific neural encoders were pretrained on thousands of hours of each participant's recordings; six participants reached personal records and one reached 11.32 BPS. Company-reported engineering update, not independent validation, peer-reviewed evidence, or regulatory approval.

INBRAIN and the MINIGRAPH consortium announced project completion: graphene probes, implant electronics, autonomous software, and a magnetic robotic implantation procedure were integrated into a functional prototype and validated in a translational model. Preclinical consortium outcome, not human implantation, regulatory clearance, or commercialization.

Announced a $45m Series A co-led by Founders Fund and The OpenAI Startup Fund for cancer-directed therapeutic neurotechnology. New round capital, not valuation or cumulative funding. Chronic human trials and FDA Breakthrough Device designation are stated goals, not completed regulatory milestones.

Announced completion of RMB 700m Series B financing, co-led by SDIC Juli, Shenzhen Capital Group and Qinzhi Capital. Approximately $105m using the Federal Reserve H.10 rate of CNY 6.6662 per USD on October 28, 2026. This is an announcement-date fallback; the actual investment date is undisclosed. Historical FX estimate, not a company-reported USD amount.

Announced a Siemens Healthineers collaboration to develop an end-to-end multimodal imaging workflow for BCI assessment, surgical planning, implantation and outcomes assessment. Development initiative, not an already deployed or cleared integrated product; Connexus remains investigational.

Announced FDA approval of a Connect-One Early Feasibility Study protocol amendment removing the four-hour-drive residence restriction for prospective participants. Travel to a study site and all other eligibility requirements still apply. Expansion of an existing IDE study, not initial IDE authorization or marketing approval.

Signed a two-year memorandum of understanding with Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, supported by the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi, for Layer 7 clinical research at its first international research site. Signing date Oct 21; company announcement Oct 29. Not a new regulatory clearance, completed efficacy result or commercial launch.

Company-reported early VOICE speech-restoration results: one participant with ALS reached 75 words per minute at 5.8% word error rate on a 125,000-word vocabulary in the first week. Disclosure/presentation date, not implantation date; preliminary single-participant evidence, not independent validation or marketing approval.

Announced a $400m Series D with participation from Khosla Ventures, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Tenet Healthcare, 885 Capital, Y Combinator, and PLC Neurotech, among others. The more than $900m raised since founding is cumulative and is not added as a round. Announcement date, not a separately disclosed closing date.
